newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom Q1 performance satisfactory-Deane.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Q1 performance satisfactory-Deane.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand's performance in the first quarter of this financial year was satisfactory in a slow economy, chief executive Roderick Deane said on Thursday.
"We are doing satisfactorily in the first quarter given the slowness of the economy," Deane told reporters after the company's annual meeting in Wellington.

Deane said the fact that Telecom had grown at several times the rate of the overall economy reflected the vigour of the industry, changes in technology and the success of Telecom's marketing activity.

"Like all other corporates that have been having difficulties in recent times in growing earnings we would like to see economic activity pick up, and one would hope that with the easing of the exchange rate a little and the easing of interest rates a little and the budget that perhaps activity will start to pick. Of course Telecom would benefit from that."
Deane said he would disappointed if Telecom could not still grow its revenues sturdily even if the economy remained flat.

"There is no question that we will capture some additional cost savings of significance as a result of that work," he said, adding that it could take a year or two for some savings to come to fruition.

Deane said Telecom was reviewing capital expenditure. Requirements had come down down from the original estimate of $800 million to "no more than $750 million and perhaps possibly significantly less than that".
He said capital laying for broadband activities comprised less than $100 million of capex. Much of the spending was concentrated in network and systems needed as a result of expanding volumes.
